next.reason: 1985 (§1985:VI.6.3.3): 'If the word immediately following NOT is GREATER, >, LESS, <, EQUAL, =, then the NOT participates as part of the relational operator'. In 2023 the NOT forms of those six operators (IS NOT GREATER THAN, IS NOT >, IS NOT LESS THAN, IS NOT <, IS NOT EQUAL TO, IS NOT =) are extended-relational-operators (§2023:8.7.5.1, rendered page 233 checked for 8.8.4.12.2), which the abbreviated format accepts before object-1 (§2023:8.8.4.12.2), and §2023:8.8.4.12.4 GR1's note says NOT 'could be as a part of an extended-relational-operator', expanding 'a > b AND NOT < c OR d' to '((a > b) AND (a NOT < c)) OR (a NOT < d)' exactly as 1985 does. Every case this rule covers (NOT followed by one of the six words) means the same; the 'otherwise' branch is 1985-GR-VI.6.3.3-L2.2.
